You also stay hands-on, personally building the models and analysis and preparing the executive-level outputs that drive investment and strategy decisions.

What you’ll do

  • M&A Strategy: Lead M&A projects end to end (owning small and mid-sized transactions independently and partnering with the Director on the largest, transformational deals), from target screening and valuation through due diligence, negotiation preparation, and post-deal integration. Run deal teams day to day, coordinate external advisors and act as the lead with target management teams or their advisors. You are not just a process manager but can form and defend a point of view on whether and why a deal makes strategic sense and present it directly to senior leadership.
  • Portfolio Optimization: Lead the strategic analysis and recommendations for key portfolio decisions, including potential geo-expansions, new vertical or brand launches or divestments.
  • Corporate Strategy: Contribute to the development of the Group's mid-term strategy by driving the process, owning the underlying analysis, strategic synthesis, and preparation of strategic documents.
  • Capital Allocation: Own and develop analytical frameworks and models to support strategic budget allocation and ROI analysis.
  • Business Unit Strategy: Act as a senior internal consultant, supporting our key business units across geographies on a project-by-project basis to develop their mid-term strategies and solve their most complex challenges.

What you’ll bring

  • Experience: 6+ years of high-performance experience from a top-tier Management Consulting firm, Investment Banking, or a comparable in-house Strategy / Corporate Development team. This includes leading projects or deal teams with minimal supervision.
  • Process and deal leadership: You have led complex, multi-stakeholder processes to a deadline, coordinating internal functions and external advisors and managing senior counterparties such as target or client management teams. This can come from running M&A transactions (in-house corporate development or advisory) or from leading strategy projects with transaction exposure, such as due diligence, carve-outs, partnerships or market entries. Direct M&A process experience is a strong plus; the ability to learn it quickly is essential.
  • Leadership and Influence: You have guided and developed more junior colleagues and influenced senior stakeholders, including through negotiation and building rapport with counterparties.
  • Toolkit: Exceptional qualitative and analytical problem-solving skills. You are hypothesis-driven and can own and structure complex analytical problems from end-to-end. You structure ambiguous problems and set direction for others, not just solve them yourself. You are utilizing AI tools to meaningfully improve your productivity. Ability to build applications with AI coding tools is a plus.
  • Financial Acumen: Expert-level financial modeling skills are required: you have built and defended complex models used for high-stakes investment or strategic decisions. Valuation experience is a plus. You are just as comfortable building analysis and models from scratch as you are managing processes and presenting recommendations to leadership.
  • DTC economics: You are comfortable working with typical DTC KPIs like CAC, AOR, AOV, CLV, retention and understand how cohort economics build a P&L over time. DTC marketing analytics experience is a plus but not required.
  • Communication: Proactive 360° communication and excellent ability to synthesize complex analysis into clear, concise storylines, presentationsand memos for an executive audience. 
  • How you work: You take ownership of outcomes and pressure-test your own conclusions before presenting them. You go deep into the analysis to get to the right answer, and know when it is good enough to decide.

  • Works with product teams where appropriate to raise product issues and provide customer feedback to help drive the product roadmap

  • Participates in product enablement sessions to learn how to best leverage new features and drive new feature enhancements adoption both internally and externally

  • Follows Professional Services best practices

  • Assists in developing and guiding customers on best practices as appropriate to the capabilities of the LM Envision platform

What You'll Need:

Must Have

  • 2+ years experience of working as an IT professional supporting one or more domains of IT infrastructure: server, network, security, storage, virtualization, cloud leveraging best practice processes such as ITIL

  • 1+ years experience in one or more programming language: Python, PowerShell, Java or Groovy

We zijn een familiebedrijf met een langetermijnvisie, waar wetenschap centraal staat in alles wat we doen. Ons verhaal begint in 1922, in Amsterdam. Vandaag, 104 jaar later en een koninklijk predicaat rijker, hoort KEUNE bij één van de hardst groeiende merken in professionele haarverzorgingsproducten. Vanuit ons hoofdkantoor in Soest worden KEUNE-producten ontwikkeld, geproduceerd en wereldwijd gedistribueerd naar meer dan 85 landen. En we zijn niet van plan om gas terug te nemen! Ieder jaar openen we een nieuwe eigen vestiging. We produceren op een duurzame en diervriendelijke manier en zijn B Corp-gecertificeerd. Maar bij KEUNE gaat het niet alleen om het creëren van mooie producten - het gaat om ons verhaal en onze visie. KEUNE staat onder leiding van Philip Berlijn, die zich richt op het bouwen van een sterk merk en het creëren van een bedrijfscultuur die draait om samenwerken, duurzaamheid en het tonen van karakter.

title: Broker Account Manager
descriptionHtml:
About Wayflyer

Today's small businesses need a capital provider that keeps pace with their growth ambitions. Traditional financing options are slow, cumbersome and often out of reach. That's why we built Wayflyer.

Our technology allows us to assess businesses in minutes, generate financing offers that reflect their growth potential and send funds in as little as 24 hours. To date, we've deployed over $6bn to thousands of businesses worldwide, backed by Tier 1 banks like J.P. Morgan.

You'll be collaborating with ambitious colleagues from around the world. We have offices in Dublin, London, New York, Charlotte, Berlin and Sydney.

 

The challenge

The Broker Channel is Wayflyer's fastest-growing route to market, and growth like that doesn't manage itself. We need someone who can scale a panel of brokers into a genuine growth engine, turning relationships and referral volume into closed deals. This isn't a maintenance role. It's a build role.

What you'll actually do

  • Grow and manage our broker panel, bringing on new brokers and training them to properly understand and sell our products

  • Build real relationships with existing brokers, the kind that make them think of you first when a deal comes up

  • Review referrals and provide sense checks and indicative offers, reading business financials well enough to spot what matters

  • Own your portfolio end to end, converting referral volume into funded deals, not just noise in the pipeline

  • Represent Wayflyer at industry events and in broker networks, building our name as much as your own

What this role could turn into

Brokers are a key focus area for the business, so whoever takes this on gets a real say in shaping it, not just executing someone else's plan. From here, that can mean leading a regional broker team as we expand into new regions, or stepping into a wider commercial partnerships role across the business.

Who thrives here

Someone who treats brokers as partners, not leads, and understands that a broker's reputation is on the line every time they refer you a deal. You're commercially sharp, comfortable with numbers, and genuinely curious about the businesses behind the applications, not just the credit markers. You don't wait for a case to be handed to you in a tidy format. You chase it down, sense-check it, and move.

We hire for range

We're looking for someone who's spent at least 2 years in business lending, ideally in fintech, and at least 2 years working directly with commercial finance brokers, with a real network to show for it. You'll have at least a year analysing business financials at a working level, and Hubspot experience is a bonus. More important than the years is the trajectory: have you built something, grown a book, or turned relationships into revenue? We'll also consider exceptional candidates from adjacent areas of business finance who don't tick every box.

Location and working policy

📍London, hybrid (3-4 days)

 

The good stuff

25 days off, plus public holidays. Private healthcare, life insurance, and a pension. Equity - because you should own a piece of what you're building. Generous parental leave for primary and secondary caregivers. 60 days a year to work abroad from wherever you want.

 

By submitting your application, you acknowledge that Wayflyer Limited will process your personal data for the purpose of evaluating your suitability for the role. Such processing is based on the need to take steps prior to entering into a potential employment agreement. To learn more about how we handle your personal data, you can contact our privacy team at https://wayflyer.com/privacy-notice.

title: Business Analyst (gn)
descriptionHtml:

Was du mitbringst

About Andercore

Andercore is the AI-native supplier of industrial materials and goods for energy and infrastructure. We execute trade and distribution end-to-end, on our own account, at the speed of compute - and we are becoming the supplier of record for the entire industry.

Industrial procurement is a €900B market in Europe alone and the largest manual market on earth. 95% of customers have no direct access to global supply chains. Materials pass through four or five intermediaries before they reach a site, and 40% of the margin evaporates on the way. For decades, the operating system of this industry was people: people to source, negotiate, finance, ship, and sell.

We built the alternative from scratch. We are the supplier. We buy from global sources and sell to European customers on our own account. Our AI runs the full trade: sourcing, quality, pricing, sales, logistics, credit, and financing. One request. A firm quote in minutes. Delivered on time. For the customer, it feels like buying from their preferred local supplier. No warehouses. No fleet. No inventory risk. Every trade is pre-sold before it is bought.

We are also the credit counterparty. Customers are scored and insured in minutes and get up to 60 days of payment terms priced into the quote itself. The working capital behind every trade is bank-funded, not equity-funded.

Where we are today:

Unternehmen wie Roche, Google, SWISS und Lonza setzen bereits auf uns. Unser Anspruch geht weiter: Wir wollen die Art verändern, wie Unternehmen Mobilität organisieren. Und wir bieten das Betriebssystem, das dies möglich macht.

Um diese Vision zu verwirklichen, suchen wir eine neugierige, unternehmerisch denkende Persönlichkeit, die Verantwortung übernimmt, Energie und gutes Urteilsvermögen mitbringt und mit uns das Unternehmen und die Mobilitätsbranche voranbringen möchte.

Deine Rolle: echte Verantwortung, spürbare Wirkung

Du möchtest ein Unternehmen mitgestalten, anspruchsvolle Probleme lösen und sehen, was deine Arbeit bewirkt.

Als Business Development Manager arbeitest du eng mit unserem Sales- und Account-Management-Team sowie mit Product, Technology und Operations zusammen. Du entwickelst aus Kundenbedürfnissen, Daten und Marktkenntnissen überzeugende Mobilitätslösungen und konkrete Wachstumschancen.

Du verantwortest Projekte, bringst eigene Ideen ein und treibst ihre Umsetzung voran. Wir erwarten, dass du von Anfang an durchdachte Fragen stellst, erkennst, wo du einen Beitrag leisten kannst, und ins Handeln kommst. Dabei unterstützen dich Kolleginnen und Kollegen, die wollen, dass du erfolgreich bist.

Was du bei uns bewegst

  • Aus Daten Chancen machen: Du analysierst Nutzungs- und Marktdaten, etwa zur Auslastung von Fahrzeugen und Parkplätzen, und entwickelst daraus umsetzbare Empfehlungen für bessere betriebliche Mobilitätslösungen.

  • Eigene Projekte vorantreiben: Du verantwortest Projekte wie Produktanalysen, die Bewertung von Geschäftschancen und die Entwicklung betrieblicher Mobilitätskonzepte. Du definierst nächste Schritte, bringst die richtigen Menschen zusammen und erzielst Ergebnisse.

  • Das Produkt verstehen: Du entwickelst ein praxisnahes Verständnis unserer Plattform, der Kundeneinrichtung, Buchungen, Abrechnungen und Integrationen. So gestaltest du Lösungen mit, die wirtschaftlich und operativ funktionieren.

  • Mit KI besser arbeiten: Du setzt KI-Tools gezielt ein, testest neue Anwendungen und verbesserst die Qualität und Effizienz unserer Recherchen, Analysen und Prozesse.

  • Wachstum vorantreiben: Du identifizierst potenzielle Kunden, verstehst ihre Herausforderungen und arbeitest mit dem Commercial-Team daran, neue Kunden zu gewinnen und bestehende Partnerschaften auszubauen.

  • Überzeugend argumentieren: Du erstellst klare Präsentationen, fundierte Business Cases, überzeugende Angebote und aussagekräftige Kundenreviews, die den Mehrwert unserer Lösungen sichtbar machen.

  • Für Fortschritt sorgen: Du setzt klare Prioritäten und hältst Kundeninformationen und nächste Schritte in HubSpot aktuell. Du hältst Zusagen ein und gehst Hindernisse frühzeitig an.

  • Teams verbinden: Du klärst technische und kommerzielle Fragen gemeinsam mit Product, Operations und Technology und leitest daraus verständliche Empfehlungen für Kunden und das Team ab.

  • Den Status quo hinterfragen: Du erkennst Verbesserungspotenzial, hinterfragst Annahmen und machst aus kreativen Ideen konkrete Verbesserungen.

Was du mitbringst

  • Einen sehr guten akademischen Leistungsausweis, beispielsweise in Betriebswirtschaft, Volkswirtschaft, Data Science oder Ingenieurwissenschaften. Wissbegierde, Kreativität und nachweisbare Leistungen sind uns wichtiger als eine bestimmte Studienrichtung.

  • Relevante praktische Erfahrung im Business Development, in der Beratung, in einem Technologieunternehmen oder im unternehmerischen Umfeld. Du kannst zeigen, welche Projekte du verantwortet und welche Ergebnisse du erzielt hast.

  • Analytisches Denkvermögen, einen sicheren Umgang mit Excel und die Fähigkeit, komplexe Ideen und Zusammenhänge zu verstehen und klar und einfach zu erklären.

  • Grosses Interesse an der Mobilität der nächsten Generation und an den Technologien, Geschäftsmodellen und Verhaltensänderungen, die die Branche prägen. Idealerweise kennst du die betriebliche Mobilitätslandschaft bereits und hast Ideen, wie sie sich verbessern lässt.

  • Gutes Urteilsvermögen: Du kannst Zielkonflikte abwägen, Wesentliches priorisieren und vorankommen, ohne auf vollständige Informationen zu warten.

  • Tatkraft und einen kreativen Zugang zur Problemlösung. Du entwickelst Vorschläge, überprüfst Annahmen und findest Wege, Dinge voranzubringen.

  • Technologieaffinität und praktische Erfahrung mit KI-Tools wie ChatGPT, Claude oder Copilot sowie das Urteilsvermögen, deren Ergebnisse kritisch zu prüfen.

  • Sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse und gute Englischkenntnisse. Französisch ist ein grosser Vorteil.

Besonders wichtig ist uns deine Haltung.

Du bringst Begeisterung, Ehrgeiz und eine lösungsorientierte Einstellung mit. Du lernst schnell, stellst durchdachte Fragen und übernimmst Verantwortung für Ergebnisse. Du achtest auf Details und suchst laufend nach Wegen, gute Arbeit noch besser zu machen.

Du bist selbstbewusst genug, eine Idee zu hinterfragen, und offen genug, deine Meinung zu ändern. Die beste Lösung und der Erfolg des Teams sind dir wichtiger als persönliche Anerkennung. Du suchst Feedback, teilst dein Wissen und arbeitest gerne mit Menschen zusammen, die das genauso halten.

Du probierst Neues aus, gehst bewusst Risiken ein und lernst aus Fehlern. Wenn du auf ein Problem stösst, ergreifst du die Initiative und beziehst andere ein, wenn es sinnvoll ist.

Was dich bei uns erwartet

Hohe Ansprüche – und kluge, herzliche Menschen, die dich fordern und weiterbringen.
Wir arbeiten ambitioniert, geben direktes, konstruktives Feedback und unterstützen uns gegenseitig. Exzellenz zeigt sich bei uns im Alltag: in durchdachten Lösungen, sorgfältiger Umsetzung und dem Willen, kontinuierlich besser zu werden.

Eine Rolle, die das ganze Unternehmen verbindet.
Du arbeitest an der Schnittstelle von Vertrieb, Customer Success, Technologie und Operations und hilfst dabei, aus Ideen Lösungen zu machen, die Kunden schätzen.

Verantwortung und Raum für Initiative.
Gute Ideen finden bei uns schnell Gehör. Du übernimmst Verantwortung dafür, Dinge voranzubringen, kannst auf die Unterstützung des Teams zählen und gestaltest mit, wie wir arbeiten.

Die Möglichkeit, mit Urban Connect zu wachsen.
Mit deinen Ergebnissen und Fähigkeiten wächst auch dein Verantwortungsbereich. Du hast die Chance, die nächste Entwicklungsphase unseres Unternehmens mitzugestalten.

Dazu kommen:

  • Flexible Arbeitszeiten und ein schönes Büro in Zürich.

  • Ein monatliches Mobilitätsbudget sowie Zugang zu unseren E-Bikes und geteilten E-Autos.

  • Ein motiviertes Team, das gerne gemeinsam und überwiegend vor Ort arbeitet, Wissen teilt und Erfolge zusammen feiert.

Bereit, etwas zu bewegen?

Schick uns deinen Lebenslauf und ein paar persönliche Zeilen: Warum Urban Connect? Was begeistert dich an der Zukunft der Mobilität? Und was hast du selbst in die Hand genommen und verbessert?

Wir freuen uns darauf, dich kennenzulernen.

title: Business Development Representative (BDR)
descriptionHtml:

Heidi Systems baut das Energy-OS für Real Estate. Dafür digitalisieren wir einen der letzten großen analogen Märkte Europas und schaffen die Infrastruktur für intelligentes Energiemanagement in Gebäuden.

Wo wir stehen:

  • Starke Pipeline mit +5.000 aktiven Deals

  • Angel-Runde mit Unicorn-Foundern sowie Directors von Google und OpenAI

  • Auf dem Weg zu 10x in 2026

Wir rollen die Messdienstbranche neu auf – einen riesigen, verstaubten Markt, den seit Jahrzehnten kaum jemand angefasst hat. Als Prop- und ClimateTech verbinden wir Software, IoT und Operations zu einer Plattform, die Energie- und Verbrauchsdaten erstmals durchgängig digital, transparent und in Echtzeit verfügbar macht. So schaffen wir die Grundlage für eine intelligente und effiziente Energieinfrastruktur von Gebäuden.

Wir wachsen stark und haben gerade unsere Angel-Runde erfolgreich abgeschlossen. Zu unseren Investoren gehören unter anderem Unicorn-Gründer sowie Directors von Google und OpenAI.

Als Founder's Associate arbeitest du direkt mit unserem Gründer Paul zusammen. Du sitzt mit uns an einem Tisch, übernimmst Verantwortung vom ersten Tag an, treibst eigene Initiativen und bringst strategische wie operative Themen wirklich ins Ziel.

Die Rolle

Als SDR bist du für viele Hausverwaltungen der erste Kontakt mit Heidi. Du findest die richtigen Ansprechpartner, führst die ersten Gespräche und sorgst dafür, dass unser Kalender mit guten Terminen voll ist.

Du arbeitest direkt mit den Gründern und unserem Sales-Team zusammen. Was du am Telefon hörst, fließt direkt in Produkt, Pitch und Preise ein.

Die Stelle passt für dich, wenn du gerade erst einsteigst, gerne telefonierst und schnell lernen willst. Uns sie passt genauso, wenn du schon ein paar Jahre Outbound im B2B gemacht hast.Je nach Erfahrung wächst die Verantwortung mit.

Deine Aufgaben

  • Du recherchierst Hausverwaltungen, Wohnungsunternehmen und Bestandshalter und findest heraus, wer bei ihnen über den Messdienst entscheidet

  • Du sprichst sie per Telefon, E-Mail und LinkedIn an und führst die ersten Gespräche

  • Du qualifizierst: Wie viele Einheiten? Wann läuft der aktuelle Vertrag aus? Wer entscheidet mit?

  • Du vereinbarst Termine und übergibst sie sauber vorbereitet an die Kollegen, die den Abschluss machen

  • Du pflegst alles in unserem CRM, damit jeder sieht, wo ein Lead steht

  • Du schaust auf deine Zahlen (Anwahlen, Gespräche, Termine, Show-Rate) und verbesserst Skripte und Sequenzen laufend

  • Du baust mit uns den Outbound-Prozess auf: Zielgruppen, Listen, Ansprache, Tools inkl. KI

  • Du bist bei Verbandsveranstaltungen und Messen der Immobilienwirtschaft mit dabei

Das bringst du mit

  • Du telefonierst gern, auch kalt, und ein Nein wirft dich nicht aus der Bahn

  • Du hörst zu, stellst gute Fragen und erklärst Dinge so, dass ein Hausverwalter mit 400 Einheiten nach 2 Minuten weiß, warum er weiter zuhören sollte

  • Du arbeitest strukturiert, setzt dir eigene Ziele und magst es, wenn Zahlen zeigen, was funktioniert

  • Du kommst gut mit Tools klar, zum Beispiel CRM, LinkedIn Sales Navigator oder KI-Tools wie ChatGPT und Claude

  • Deutsch auf C2-Niveau, schriftlich und mündlich

  • Erste Erfahrung in Vertrieb, Kundenkontakt oder Call-Center ist super. Wenn du schon 1 bis 3 Jahre B2B-Outbound gemacht hast, umso besser. Quereinsteiger sind ausdrücklich willkommen

Benefits

  • Direkte Zusammenarbeit und tägliches Mentoring durch einen erfahrenen Gründer und eine extrem steile Lernkurve

  • Teil eines stark wachsenden Early-Stage-Startups zu werden, das einen riesigen Markt digitalisiert – mit viel Eigenverantwortung, hoher Geschwindigkeit und echtem Gestaltungsspielraum

  • Die Chance, echten Impact zu erzielen – an einem der größten, aber oft unterschätzten Hebel der Energiewende: Mit digitalen Messdienstleistungen schaffen wir die Grundlage für effizientere Gebäude und messbare CO₂-Einsparungen

  • Bei sehr guter Performance besteht eine klare Übernahmeoption und die Möglichkeit, Heidi als einer der ersten 20 Mitarbeitenden langfristig mit aufzubauen

  • Ein High-Performance-Team in einer humorvollen und unterstützenden Kultur, mit regelmäßigen Team-Dinnern und gemeinsamen Events

  • Ein neu renoviertes Altbau-Office in Berlin Mitte direkt am Monbijoupark, gemeinsames Arbeiten an einem Tisch, kurze Wege und direkte Entscheidungen

  • Zugang zu einem starken Netzwerk in Immobilien, Tech, Energie und Venture Capital

title: CAM Programmer
descriptionHtml:
About Isembard

Isembard is building a network of high-performance factories for critical industries. We combine advanced machine tools, robotics and our own software, MasonOS, to make precision components for aerospace, defence, energy and frontier technology companies, with factories across the UK, US, Germany and France. Our mission is to forge industrial acceleration.

The role

CAM programming connects the drawing to repeatable precision production. Our central CAM team in London programmes parts for factories across the network, and how many new parts we can take on depends on it.

You will own programming and machining standards from toolpath to prove-out, support complex parts, and write the methods and libraries other sites reuse.

What you'll do

  • Programme, simulate and optimise 3-axis and 5-axis milling.

  • Prove out first articles to aerospace and defence standards.

  • Choose tooling, cutting parameters and work-holding for aluminium, steels, titanium and Inconel.

  • Drive cycle time and machine utilisation.

  • Standardise programmes across our UK factories, and maintain toolpath libraries, templates and documentation.

What we're looking for

  • Strong CAM programming in Hypermill (preferred), Mastercam, Siemens NX or equivalent.

  • A record of holding ±0.01 mm or tighter.

  • Experience setting and running high-end machines in production, such as Hermle or DMG Mori, across a multi-machine environment.

  • A solid understanding of feeds, speeds, tooling strategy and work-holding, based on reasoning rather than habit.

  • Confident interpretation of complex drawings and GD&T.

Nice to have

  • Aerospace or defence manufacturing experience.

  • 5-axis simultaneous machining.

  • Titanium and high-strength alloys.

  • NC simulation such as Vericut, and probing or pallet systems.

  • EN 9100 or AS9100 familiarity.

Why Isembard

  • Set programming standards the whole network reuses.

  • Work on advanced machine tools on parts that matter.

  • Competitive salary and equity.

Location: On-site at our Southwark factory in London, with visits to other UK sites. This is a hands-on factory role: you programme it, prove it and help run it.

Nice-to-Have (Not Required)

  • Familiarity with the hospitality or restaurant industry.

  • Exposure to SaaS, payments, or banking/lending products.

Come live the Lightspeed experience...

  • Unlock your potential with our growth program, paving the way for promotions and career advancement;

  • Genuine career opportunities in a company that’s creating new jobs every day;

  • Work in a team big enough for growth but lean enough to make a real impact.

… and enjoy a range of benefits that’ll keep you happy, healthy and (not) hungry:

Lightspeed is a proud equal opportunity employer and we are committed to creating an inclusive and barrier-free workplace. Lightspeed welcomes and encourages applications from people with disabilities. Accommodations are available on request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the selection process.

Where to from here?

Obviously, this has to be mutually beneficial: we want you to step into a role you love, and we want to offer you a place you’re proud to come to every day. For a glimpse into our world check out our career page here.

Lightspeed is building communities through commerce, and we need people from all backgrounds and lived experiences to do that. We were founded in 2005, in Montreal’s gay village and our original members were all part of the LGBTQ+ community. The ethos of our business has been about inclusion from the very beginning, and we strive to provide a workplace where everyone belongs.

Who we are:

Powering the businesses that are the backbone of the global economy, Lightspeed's one-stop commerce platform helps merchants innovate to simplify, scale, and provide exceptional customer experiences. Founded in Montréal, Canada in 2005, Lightspeed is dual-listed on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE: LSPD) and Toronto Stock Exchange (TSX: LSPD). With teams across North America, Europe, and Asia Pacific, the company serves retail, hospitality, and golf businesses in over 100 countries.

title: Chief Customer Officer
descriptionHtml:
Work from anywhere, impact everywhere

Diversity is at the heart of who we are at Xapo Bank.
We're a fully distributed team of over 160 Xapiens that work remotely from 50+ countries around the world.

Our beginning: A world that enjoys economic freedom and wealth protection,no matter where you live or who is running your country.
To achieve that, we search the world for the best people for the job.
We work hard, think globally, and inspire each other to learn and grow.
We are committed to changing the way things are done.

Although we are headquartered in Gibraltar, this is a full time, 100% remote position
Work from anywhere!

Position overview

Xapo's product suite has grown from a Bitcoin vault into a full member proposition: BTC and USD accounts that pay interest, a global card with Bitcoin cashback, Bitcoin-backed loans, a growing suite of BTC wealth and credit products, and access to stocks, ETFs, and stablecoins, all inside one regulated relationship.

Xapo is a bank, and a bank earns on the money its members choose to hold with it. Each of those products shipped well. What hasn't yet existed is a single owner of the economics of the customer relationship: one person accountable for winning the right members, growing what they hold with us, and keeping them, and for the balance-sheet products that make that possible.

The Chief Customer Officer is a new role at the top of the house, reporting to the CEO. You will run the stream that grows what members hold with Xapo, and you will own the Customer P&L, retail and institutional. It brings growth, client coverage, product management, and product design under one leader who is judged on customer contribution, the assets attracted and kept, and the members who stay. This is a customer-focused role in the most commercial sense: what a member earns from us, not the feature we shipped, is the centre of every decision.

The measure of success is a Customer P&L that grows on what members hold and keep: LTV:CAC improving, approved-to-paid rising, churn falling, and customer contribution the business can plan against.

This is a banking role, not a requirements-gathering role, a marketing role, or a role you can run from a dashboard. Products are priced on the balance sheet and judged on the money they attract and keep.

The mandate

  1. Own the Customer P&L, retail and institutional.
    You own customer contribution: customer gross profit from what members' balances earn, secured lending, Bitcoin yield, and conversion, stocks and ETFs, less the cost of winning and keeping members. We earn on what members hold, not on what they tap, send, or click, so you run on assets held and the margin they earn, not payment volume. Good looks like a Customer P&L the Exco and Board can plan against, where every line has a number you own and can explain, up or down.
  2. Grow what members hold with us, through earning products run like a banker would.
    You own the roadmap for the balance-sheet products: deposits and savings, lending and credit, and trading and structured. Each is led by a mission PM who is a banker, owning a product's contribution and its price on the balance sheet, not a backlog. Requirements go through the gate; the economics are the job. Every item is priced by Finance before it is built, on a shared risk appetite with Risk and Treasury. Good looks like products that scale assets held and member lifetime value at a risk profile the Board actually approved.
  3. Win the right members, efficiently.
    You own Growth: audience, lifecycle, and content, with one head accountable for the path from approval to paid. You own CAC and approved-to-paid, find the members who bring other members, and activate them in week one. Every incentive is priced before it runs. Good looks like net paid-member growth that improves every quarter, at a CAC that LTV comfortably justifies, because you diagnosed where the funnel leaks rather than spending more to fill it.
  4. Keep members, and deepen the relationship with the ones who hold balances.
    Retention is the most efficient growth we have. You own churn, and you own Client Coverage: relationship managers who sell the missions' products to the members who hold balances, and loop demand back into the roadmap. You are accountable for net new AUM flow, covered-book retention, and products per covered member, and for growth that is broad-based rather than concentrated in a few accounts. Good looks like falling churn and AUM growth from members who stay and expand rather than members re-acquired at cost.
  5. Make the value of Xapo visible, and the experience effortless.
    You own Product Design: one design system and one shell, so that members see the value of what they are earning clearly and early, and find every task simple. You design the proposition in the stream with Finance and partner with Operations, who run onboarding, KYC, support, cards, and payments, to remove friction at the points that affect members most. Good looks like members who understand their return, complete what they set out to do, and stay.
  6. Build one Customer organisation, not four.
    Growth, Client Coverage, Mission PMs, and Product Design come together under one operating model: one set of key results read weekly from one source, shared frameworks for discovery and prioritisation, and real career paths for the people in it. Engineering is pulled to a single ranked roadmap, and nobody in your line has engineers of their own. Good looks like fewer hand-offs per outcome and a number for every cell that its owner explains every week.
  7. Bring the regulated-bank and crypto-native lens to every customer call.
    You understand that a KYC onboarding decision and an AML monitoring decision carry different risk appetites, that a false positive at the gate is a paid-for member lost, and that a proposition built for a crypto-native power user can still fail a first-time bank customer. You can sit in the same room as a CRO, an MLRO, a CFO, and an engineering lead and make a customer case that survives all four conversations.

How you'll operate

This part matters as much as the mandate. The known failure mode for this role, in any company, is a CCO with a polished customer-insight deck and no ownership of the number. That is disqualifying here.

  • You lead from inside the work. You sit in on growth reviews, mission PM reviews, client meetings, and member calls, not just steering committees. PMs, designers, and relationship managers three levels down know your name because you've solved problems with them.
  • You move people with the business case, not the whip. When a priority needs to change, you diagnose the problem, build the case with data and the economics, and show teams why it matters, so they re-prioritise because they're convinced, not because they were told. Your authority comes from being right and being useful, not from your title.
  • You have extreme ownership. You own the Customer P&L and the member metrics beneath it, not the feature ship date. If a launch didn't move contribution, LTV:CAC, approved-to-paid, or churn, you don't report "the roadmap item shipped", you change the approach.
  • You have genuine gravitas. Senior, experienced leaders welcome your input because you've earned the standing to give it. You can challenge any executive's plan, including the CEO's, constructively, with evidence, and be thanked for it, because your challenge makes their work stronger.
  • You diagnose before you prescribe. You can walk into a leaking funnel, a churning segment, or a product that isn't earning and find the structural cause, then fix the economics, not just the symptom.

What you'll have done

  • 10+ years in senior commercial or customer leadership (CCO, Chief Growth or Commercial Officer, MD or Head of Retail or Wealth, or equivalent) in digital banking, fintech, or payments, including meaningful time in a regulated environment (banking licence, e-money, or equivalent prudential/conduct regime).
  • Crypto-native credibility: hands-on experience building and growing customer propositions on or around digital assets, custody, on-chain flows, Bitcoin-backed lending, or similar. You don't need Bitcoin explained to you, and you don't need banking explained to you either.
  • Customer P&L ownership: you have owned a customer or product P&L judged on contribution, balances, and margin rather than transaction volume, and you are fluent in NIM, unit economics, customer contribution, and LTV:CAC.
  • Growth and lifecycle: a track record of acquiring, activating, and retaining members in a regulated, KYC-heavy environment, improving approved-to-paid and churn while holding CAC to a level that LTV justifies, not just growth-hacking a free consumer app.
  • Banking-grade product leadership: you have led product management for balance-sheet products such as savings, lending, or structured products, priced with Finance, with PMs who own a product's economics rather than a backlog. Experience with client coverage or relationship-managed models for high-balance and institutional clients is a strong advantage.
  • Commercial and risk fluency: you can build a customer business case that survives scrutiny from Finance, Risk, and Compliance in the same meeting, and you know the difference between growth that's sustainable and growth that's borrowed from tomorrow's risk appetite.
  • A track record of outcomes you can narrate: specific LTV:CAC, approved-to-paid, churn, AUM, or contribution numbers you owned, bets you killed when the data didn't support them, and outcomes you can prove.

The first 90 days

Day 30: The Customer P&L baseline is documented across retail and institutional: customer contribution, LTV:CAC, approved-to-paid, churn, net paid-member growth, and assets attracted and kept. You have formed your own independent view of where members are won, lost, and under-served, and shared it with the CEO and Board.Day 60: The unified Customer operating model is live: one set of key results across Growth, Client Coverage, Mission PMs, and Product Design, read weekly from one source. Every mission PM owns a product's contribution and its price, and the roadmap is ranked on what it earns, built with Finance and the line leads.Day 90: At least one measurable improvement in LTV:CAC, approved-to-paid, churn, or net new AUM flow is live and attributable to a change you made, not a feature ship, an outcome moved. Every cell in your line has defined key results and an owner who explains the number every week.

What this role is not

  • Not a requirements-gathering role. Mission PMs are bankers who own a product's contribution and price, not a backlog. You partner with Technology, Finance, and Operations on execution; you don't run those functions.
  • Not a volume role. If your primary output is card spend, transfer volume, or a shipped list rather than assets held and the margin they earn, we have both failed.
  • Not a reporting layer. If your primary output is a customer-insight deck or a roadmap deck, we have both failed.
  • Not a role that can be done from a distance. Remote-first means distributed, not detached.

Other requirements

  • A dedicated workspace.
  • A reliable internet connection with the fastest speed possible in your area.
  • Alignment with Our Values and the Xapo Values-Driven Leadership principles.

Why work for Xapo?

Impact Globally, Work Remotely.

  • Shape the Future
    Improve lives through cutting-edge technology, work 100% remotely from anywhere in the world.

  • Great work-life balance
    Build amazing things with a balance of autonomy and collaborative teamwork. Set your own work schedule and make use of a flexible PTO plan when you need to recharge.

  • Expect Excellence
    Collaborate, learn, and grow with a high-performance team. Learn how you learn best - from books to conferences, you'll get a yearly budget for your individual learning and development goals.

At Xapo, we prioritize consumer protection and adhere to regulatory requirements by ensuring that all Xapiens are accountable for upholding principles of fair treatment, transparency, and ethical conduct in their interactions with customers and stakeholders.

  • You lead from inside the work. You sit in on growth reviews, mission PM reviews, client meetings, and member calls, not just steering committees. PMs, designers, and relationship managers three levels down know your name because you've solved problems with them.
  • You move people with the business case, not the whip. When a priority needs to change, you diagnose the problem, build the case with data and the economics, and show teams why it matters, so they re-prioritise because they're convinced, not because they were told. Your authority comes from being right and being useful, not from your title.
  • You have extreme ownership. You own the Customer P&L and the member metrics beneath it, not the feature ship date. If a launch didn't move contribution, LTV:CAC, approved-to-paid, or churn, you don't report "the roadmap item shipped", you change the approach.
  • You have genuine gravitas. Senior, experienced leaders welcome your input because you've earned the standing to give it. You can challenge any executive's plan, including the CEO's, constructively, with evidence, and be thanked for it, because your challenge makes their work stronger.
  • You diagnose before you prescribe. You can walk into a leaking funnel, a churning segment, or a product that isn't earning and find the structural cause, then fix the economics, not just the symptom.

What you'll have done

  • 10+ years in senior commercial or customer leadership (CCO, Chief Growth or Commercial Officer, MD or Head of Retail or Wealth, or equivalent) in digital banking, fintech, or payments, including meaningful time in a regulated environment (banking licence, e-money, or equivalent prudential/conduct regime).
  • Crypto-native credibility: hands-on experience building and growing customer propositions on or around digital assets, custody, on-chain flows, Bitcoin-backed lending, or similar. You don't need Bitcoin explained to you, and you don't need banking explained to you either.
  • Customer P&L ownership: you have owned a customer or product P&L judged on contribution, balances, and margin rather than transaction volume, and you are fluent in NIM, unit economics, customer contribution, and LTV:CAC.
  • Growth and lifecycle: a track record of acquiring, activating, and retaining members in a regulated, KYC-heavy environment, improving approved-to-paid and churn while holding CAC to a level that LTV justifies, not just growth-hacking a free consumer app.
  • Banking-grade product leadership: you have led product management for balance-sheet products such as savings, lending, or structured products, priced with Finance, with PMs who own a product's economics rather than a backlog. Experience with client coverage or relationship-managed models for high-balance and institutional clients is a strong advantage.
  • Commercial and risk fluency: you can build a customer business case that survives scrutiny from Finance, Risk, and Compliance in the same meeting, and you know the difference between growth that's sustainable and growth that's borrowed from tomorrow's risk appetite.
  • A track record of outcomes you can narrate: specific LTV:CAC, approved-to-paid, churn, AUM, or contribution numbers you owned, bets you killed when the data didn't support them, and outcomes you can prove.

The first 90 days

Day 30: The Customer P&L baseline is documented across retail and institutional: customer contribution, LTV:CAC, approved-to-paid, churn, net paid-member growth, and assets attracted and kept. You have formed your own independent view of where members are won, lost, and under-served, and shared it with the CEO and Board.Day 60: The unified Customer operating model is live: one set of key results across Growth, Client Coverage, Mission PMs, and Product Design, read weekly from one source. Every mission PM owns a product's contribution and its price, and the roadmap is ranked on what it earns, built with Finance and the line leads.Day 90: At least one measurable improvement in LTV:CAC, approved-to-paid, churn, or net new AUM flow is live and attributable to a change you made, not a feature ship, an outcome moved. Every cell in your line has defined key results and an owner who explains the number every week.

What this role is not

  • Not a requirements-gathering role. Mission PMs are bankers who own a product's contribution and price, not a backlog. You partner with Technology, Finance, and Operations on execution; you don't run those functions.
  • Not a volume role. If your primary output is card spend, transfer volume, or a shipped list rather than assets held and the margin they earn, we have both failed.
  • Not a reporting layer. If your primary output is a customer-insight deck or a roadmap deck, we have both failed.
  • Not a role that can be done from a distance. Remote-first means distributed, not detached.

Other requirements

  • A dedicated workspace.
  • A reliable internet connection with the fastest speed possible in your area.
  • Alignment with Our Values and the Xapo Values-Driven Leadership principles.

Why work for Xapo?

Impact Globally, Work Remotely.

  • Shape the Future
    Improve lives through cutting-edge technology, work 100% remotely from anywhere in the world.

  • Great work-life balance
    Build amazing things with a balance of autonomy and collaborative teamwork. Set your own work schedule and make use of a flexible PTO plan when you need to recharge.

  • Expect Excellence
    Collaborate, learn, and grow with a high-performance team. Learn how you learn best - from books to conferences, you'll get a yearly budget for your individual learning and development goals.

At Xapo, we prioritize consumer protection and adhere to regulatory requirements by ensuring that all Xapiens are accountable for upholding principles of fair treatment, transparency, and ethical conduct in their interactions with customers and stakeholders.

title: Clinical Solutions Consultant
descriptionHtml:
About Rivia

Rivia is a technology company building a data engine that powers the future of clinical trial intelligence. Rivia was founded on the belief that new drugs can be brought to market more successfully with a fraction of today's capital.

Biotechs are the source of most therapeutic innovation, yet clinical development is constantly constrained by fragmented data and outdated tooling. Rivia unifies clinical trial data at scale through a core engine built as a reusable intelligence layer, comprising hundreds of configurations and trial-specific logic, independent of source structure. This vertical stack of data engine, workflows, and agents creates a distinct advantage in how trials are operated.

Over the past two years, European- and US-based biotechs running global clinical trials on Rivia have demonstrated measurable impact, from earlier understanding of therapeutic potential to significantly more efficient trial execution. In March 2026, Rivia raised its $15M Series A led by Earlybird Venture Capital.

Rivia's ambition is to become the standard infrastructure for modern drug development, transforming how trials are executed end-to-end.

The Role

As our Clinical Solutions Consultant, you'll be the bridge between science, technology, and sales, helping biotech and pharma companies understand how Rivia can transform the way they work with clinical trial data.

You'll partner closely with our Account Executives throughout the technical stages of the sales cycle, turning complex scientific and technical challenges into compelling product demonstrations, tailored sandboxes, and solutions that address real customer needs.

This isn't a role where you simply present slides or follow a demo script. You'll need to understand clinical trial workflows, get hands-on with data, challenge assumptions, and translate complex customer requirements into solutions we can actually deliver.

You'll also play an important role in shaping how we approach technical pre-sales at Rivia, building repeatable processes, improving our demo environments, and helping us scale without losing the scientific depth and customer understanding that make us different.

What Excites You

  • Bringing science and technology together: You love understanding complex scientific challenges and translating them into practical, impactful solutions.

  • Being hands-on: You don't just talk about what a product can do. You enjoy building demos, configuring sandboxes, working with data, and showing customers what's possible.

  • Making an impact on revenue: You enjoy being part of the sales process, influencing strategic deals, and helping customers confidently make decisions.

  • Solving real customer problems: You're curious about how biotech and pharma companies operate and enjoy finding creative ways to address their challenges.

  • Building from the ground up: You get excited about joining a growing company where you can shape processes, improve tools, and help establish how technical pre-sales should work.

  • Working across teams: You enjoy collaborating with Sales, Product, and Engineering, balancing commercial opportunities with technical feasibility.

Responsibilities

  • Partner with Account Executives as the scientific and technical expert throughout the sales process, helping prospects understand how Rivia can address their specific challenges.

  • Lead in-depth product demonstrations tailored to customers' clinical trial workflows, data structures, and scientific requirements.

  • Build and configure customized sandboxes, demo environments, and prototype integrations to demonstrate Rivia's value using realistic customer scenarios.

  • Understand customers' clinical trial pipelines, protocols, endpoints, and data challenges, translating their needs into practical technical solutions.

  • Scope prospective customer implementations, identifying technical requirements, dependencies, risks, and feasibility before commercial commitments are made.

  • Collaborate closely with Solutions Engineers and Customer Engagement to ensure smooth handovers from pre-sales to implementation.

  • Act as a trusted technical advisor to both customers and internal teams, confidently addressing complex scientific questions while being transparent about product capabilities and limitations.

  • Adapt demonstrations and technical conversations to customers' familiarity with and readiness to adopt AI-driven solutions.

  • Identify recurring customer needs, technical objections, and product gaps, sharing insights with Product and Engineering to continuously improve our offering.

  • Help develop scalable pre-sales processes, reusable demo environments, and technical documentation as Rivia grows.

What Excites Us

  • Scientific background: You have a degree in life sciences, bioinformatics, biomedical engineering, or a related scientific discipline, and you're comfortable navigating complex scientific discussions.

  • Relevant experience: You bring at least 4 years of client-facing experience in solutions consulting, technical pre-sales, field application science, technical account management, or similar roles.

  • Scientific and technical fluency: You understand scientific data and experimental logic, and can quickly grasp complex clinical trial workflows and technical requirements.

  • Hands-on technical skills: You've personally built and configured product demos, sandboxes, or technical proof-of-concepts, rather than only presenting solutions developed by others.

  • Commercial mindset: You understand how technical expertise contributes to winning deals and enjoy working closely with sales teams to move opportunities forward.

  • Customer-facing confidence: You can communicate complex technical concepts clearly and credibly, whether you're speaking with scientists, clinical operations leaders, or technical stakeholders.

  • Strong ownership: You're proactive, independent, and comfortable operating in a fast-moving environment where processes are still being built.

  • Collaborative approach: You know when to challenge assumptions, push back on unrealistic commitments, and work across teams to deliver the best outcomes for customers.

Bonus / Nice to Have

  • Previous experience in scientific software, clinical trial technology, biotech platforms, or laboratory informatics.

  • Familiarity with clinical trial protocols, endpoints, regulatory considerations, and clinical data integration.

  • Experience working with AI-driven products or communicating the value of AI to scientific and technical stakeholders.

Our Values

  • In It to Win It: Approach every challenge with determination, resilience, and a drive to achieve the best possible outcomes.

  • Embrace Change: We see change as an opportunity for growth, innovation, and improvement, continuously evolving to stay one step ahead.

  • Why Not?: We challenge assumptions, stay curious, and explore new possibilities rather than accepting things as they are.

  • Find the Gap: We proactively identify opportunities, anticipate challenges, and solve problems before they arise.

  • Collective Accountability: We're one team, on one mission, committed to shared responsibility, mutual support, and trust.

  • Value Add Solutions: Know better. Act better. We're dedicated to delivering meaningful solutions that create real impact.

We are looking for a Cloud Engineer (m/f/d) to join us in Hamburg or Siegen and build and operate the scalable, secure cloud platform that connects users with our trapped-ion quantum computers.

Responsibilities:

You will join our Quantum firmware Team as a Cloud Engineer. You will build the layer through which the world reaches our quantum computers. Users submit quantum programs; your services compile, schedule, and dispatch them to our machines and return the results:

  • Build and operate the cloud services that let users submit quantum programs to our systems and retrieve their results.

  • Develop and deploy our compilation pipeline as a scalable cloud service , from circuit input through transpilation down to hardware-level instructions

  • Design and maintain the public API and SDK entry points to our platform

  • Guarantee tenant isolation, so that quantum programs and results are never visible across customer boundaries, and manage secrets and credentials across the stack

  • Instrument the platform for observability and keep an eye on latency, throughput, and cost


Required Skills:

  • 3+ years of hands-on experience building and deploying backend or platform services in production

  • Strong Python; additional systems-level language experience (Go, Rust, C++) is welcome

  • Solid API design skills (REST and/or gRPC) for services other developers have to use

  • Practical experience implementing authentication and authorisation in production systems: OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect, token handling, and role-based access control

  • Secure engineering habits: least privilege by default, proper secrets management, and awareness of dependency and container supply-chain risks

  • Infrastructure as code (Terraform, Pulumi, or similar) and CI/CD pipelines (GitLab CI, GitHub Actions, or similar)

  • Working understanding of GDPR and data residency requirements, and a genuine interest in digital sovereignty

If you’re moving from another country to join Picnic we make it as smooth as possible for you. We’ll cover your flight costs and a first month's accommodation. 

 🥗Fresh Lunch, coffee, and snacks 

Our offices are equipped with fully-fledged coffee bars and a kitchen. We get delicious fresh and warm lunches every day so you can keep your energy up.

⛳All the rest 

At Picnic you get 30 holidays, we cover your travel expenses and offer a pension plan. And your phone and laptop are on us, of course.

FAQ

Which team will I join?

At Picnic, we build almost everything in-house. This means that we have plenty of opportunities for you in terms of project topics. Your interest lies in consumer topics like pricing, assortment, customer life time value? Or rather in logistics, supply chain, automated warehousing areas? Or you'd love going adventurous into new areas as long as you're solving real world problems? Let's talk and figure it out where there's the best match.  

What are the long term opportunities for this role? What happens after I'm done with a project?

You get full accountability from the start: from shaping the strategy and driving step-change improvements, to collaborating with multiple teams to achieve tangible business results.

At Picnic, the long-term opportunity isn't just a role—it’s a platform to shape your own career trajectory with real ownership, business impact, and fast growth. Hence the career paths are as diverse as your ambitions. Depending on your interests and strengths, these are most common career paths we’ve seen so far:

  • Given our scale-up environment, many projects tend to grow in scope and complexity under your responsibility and you naturally grow a team around you in order to take your project to a next level.
  • As you grow, you’ll deepen your understanding of the business, build a strong internal network, and prove your ability to lead impactful projects. Once you feel you’ve learned everything in your scope and your projects have been successfully implemented, you can switch to complete different areas of Picnic. We have numerous colleagues that have switched from Commercial to Fulfillment, or from Distribution to Customer and many other examples.

In what language should I apply?

Please send your application in English.

title: Commercial Contracts Associate (NDA)
descriptionHtml:
About Norm Ai
Norm Ai, the agentic law company, has a client base with a combined $30 trillion in assets under management.


Norm Ai pioneered Legal Engineering, the process that empowers lawyers to build and supervise domain-specific AI agents with Norm’s proprietary suite of no-code software tools. Norm Ai technology is deployed inside many of the largest and most consequential institutions in the world.


Norm Ai is also the technology behind Norm Law, LLP, a separate but affiliated AI-native law firm built for the era of agentic AI. Norm Law’s attorneys advise leading institutions across private funds, private equity, venture capital, real estate, registered funds, and financial regulation, using the same legal intelligence platform that powers Norm Ai’s products.

AI Fluency:
Norm Ai prefers all team members to be fluent in AI. Successful candidates actively use AI in their day-to-day work to support thinking, creation, and problem-solving. They use it to improve the quality and speed of their work and to continuously refine how work gets done end-to-end.

Candidates should be prepared to demonstrate and discuss their AI usage throughout the interview process, including concrete examples of tools, workflows, and outcomes. We look for practical, hands-on experience, not theoretical familiarity.

This Role

As a Commercial Contracts Associate (NDA), you will work on a high impact team that provides important services to Norm Law’s clients, while using AI agents to streamline the drafting, review, and execution process in providing non-disclosure agreement review for clients. You’ll collaborate closely with partners, clients, and technology teams to deliver efficient, precise, and data-driven legal services for in-house legal teams of leading asset managers.

Our practice embraces the use of AI to reduce burden and increase your ability to focus on strategic legal judgment and client engagement.

What You'll Do

  • Document Drafting, Review, and Negotiation: Leverage AI agents to generate, compare, negotiate, and redline NDAs tailored to client guidelines

  • Incorporating Legal Context: Advise clients on their NDA playbooks and market standards, including ensuring AI agents understand each client's specific context and comparing client’s actual practices with playbook positions in order to guide updates.

  • NDA Execution: Integrate AI agents into workflow management, execution, negotiation, and coordination with counterparties for any NDAs.

  • Client Advisory: Partner with clients to demonstrate how AI-assisted workflows improve accuracy, transparency, and velocity.

  • Collaboration with Tech: Work closely with the technology teams to continue to make the NDA review process even more efficient using AI.

  • Managing high volumes of requests: Maintain a tracker, manage multiple high priority requests simultaneously and communicate timing expectations to clients and consistently and proactively follow up and move negotiations forward.

What We're Looking For

Core Qualifications

  • Qualified solicitor admitted in England and Wales, with a current Solicitors Regulation Authority (SRA) practising certificate.

  • 2-3+ years of experience reviewing NDAs or similar agreements.

  • Strong drafting and communication skills; meticulous attention to detail.

  • Interest in applying technology to enhance traditional deal workflows.

What Success Looks Like

  • 30 Days: Learn firm AI platforms; begin supporting the commercial contracts team using AI-enabled review and drafting.

  • 60 Days: Independently manage discrete components of NDA review with AI support.

  • 90 Days: Lead AI-augmented workstreams in live NDA reviews, improving efficiency and accuracy in document management and execution processes.

Benefits

Benefits: pension plan with an employer contribution, medical and dental insurance coverage, employee referral bonus program, initial 2 week onboarding in the US.

Work Location

Location: Central London

Work model: Hybrid

In-office expectation: 4-5 days per week

Why Join Norm Law

You’ll be part of the founding UK team bringing a proven US category leader to a receptive UK market. You’ll have autonomy, visibility, and the opportunity to build meaningful relationships — backed by a world-class product, an experienced executive team, and a growing global reputation.

To learn more about Norm Ai, visit our website.

title: Commercial Lead UK
descriptionHtml:
About Klim

The team at Klim is building the operating system for regenerative agriculture. We help farms restore their soil - and turn that into real, measurable business value for the food companies, banks and insurers who depend on it.

We’re a Berlin-based agritech startup backed by $22M in Series A funding, partnering with global food leaders such as Nestlé and ADM to build supply chain resilience through regenerative agriculture. Since 2020, we’ve supported +4,000 farmers managing over 900,000 hectares.

Join our incredible team of 80+ dedicated people across Germany, the UK, Poland and Czechia to help build a more sustainable, resilient food system and drive real climate impact.

Your mission

As our Commercial Lead, you will be responsible for growing Klim's business in the UK. You'll source, win and expand partnerships with a wide variety of food companies operating in the UK, helping them build more profitable, resilient supply chains, and scale Klim’s business in a key strategic market.

You'll build our UK sales pipeline and help grow our presence in the market with a focus on generating leads, scoping consultative programmes, negotiating partnerships and managing key customer relationships.

You'll also play a leading role in identifying market opportunities, customer needs and emerging trends that can inform Klim’s UK strategy, go-to-market engine, marketing, and product roadmap.

This role is based in the UK, and we have a coworking space in London where the team meets to collaborate. Expect mostly UK-based travel, with occasional trips to our Berlin office for company-wide get-togethers.

What you'll do:

  • Shape our UK go-to-market strategy: define target accounts, account plans and pricing within Klim’s standard offering. Help lead our marketing and communications strategy, build our brand and reputation, and bring customer feedback into product and strategy.

  • Own the end-to-end enterprise sales cycle: guide CPGs, retailers, agri-traders and other businesses from outreach, discovery and qualification through to programme design, proposals, negotiation and signed contracts. Help stakeholders across finance, procurement and sustainability understand how soil regeneration supports Scope 3 reduction, supply chain resilience, lower sourcing risk and enterprise value.

  • Build UK partnerships: develop relationships with complementary businesses, grain traders, agronomy businesses and industry bodies that connect Klim with UK farmers and buyers.

  • Grow lasting customer relationships: develop initial programmes into larger, multi-year partnerships across commodities and sourcing regions. Collaborate with our internal teams to deliver successful programmes and support renewals.

  • Turn market insights into action: stay up to date with regulatory developments, competitors, industry trends and standards. Use this knowledge to advise customers and identify opportunities for Klim’s UK business.

You’ll be responsible for UK new business and account growth, reporting directly to Rory Davidson, UK Country Lead & Head of Marketing.

What success looks like after 12 months:

  • Revenue targets met: Target of net new UK contract value closed.

  • Pipeline targets met: a qualified UK pipeline target met, implementing a MEDDPICC sales motion

  • Expansion targets met: top UK accounts grown into larger or multi-year programmes.

  • New logos: Target of net new UK enterprise clients signed from our target ICPs

  • Market presence & reputation: Klim recognised as a credible voice on regenerative supply chains by UK buyers, partners & industry bodies


What you bring -

Must have:

You’re deeply motivated to grow Klim’s business in the UK and take it to the next level.

  • Location: You are based in the UK and have the right to work there.

  • Consulting or Enterprise sales: You have 5+ years in consulting and/or enterprise B2B sales, business development or client-facing leadership roles. You have a track record of scoping and leading large complex projects, and / or closing complex, 6- and 7-figure deals with a technical element (preferably within sustainability or procurement)

  • P&L Impact: Demonstrated experience developing and closing commercial partnerships, contracts, or other revenue-generating opportunities.

  • Sector depth: You have experience in the UK agri-food system - e.g. agri-food sustainability, agritech, soil carbon or MRV, agronomy & inputs, or food & drink supply chains.

  • Consultative approach: you diagnose before you pitch, build the business case together with the customer, and are comfortable managing different stakeholders - including senior finance and procurement leaders. Consulting experience is preferred.

  • Sales discipline: Experience with a structured sales method such as MEDDPIC, and CRM tools such as Pipedrive.

  • Ownership: Excited to lead and build out a market with a small local team, with a larger cross-functional support team behind you.

  • Communication: Used to preparing high quality client-facing materials, and confident presenting to boards and at industry events.

Nice to have:

  • A background in management or sustainability consulting

  • Working knowledge of regenerative agriculture, Scope 3 accounting (e.g. SBTi FLAG, GHG Protocol) or UK agricultural policy

title: Conversion Manager - Financial Services
descriptionHtml:
Why This Role Exists

At Pennylane, our website plays a pivotal role in acquiring and converting customers, transforming traffic from paid acquisition, SEO, partnerships, and other channels into sign-ups, demo bookings, and product adoption.

 

As we accelerate our Financial Services offering, including pro account, and the monetization of our existing customer base, we are seeking a Conversion Manager to own conversion across these strategic areas.

 

You will lead the production and optimization of website pages and paid landing pages, from identifying friction to measuring business impact.

 

You will join the Website team within Growth and collaborate closely with Growth Engineers and Data in a multidisciplinary squad.

 

🌍 About Pennylane

Pennylane is one of France’s leading fintech unicorns, building the financial and accounting operating system for European SMEs and accounting firms.

 

Founded in 2020, we help business owners make better decisions and empower accountants to focus on advising their clients.

 

Key Figures and Ambition

  • 💻 Over 1.3 million SMEs already work with Pennylane

  • 🤝 More than 7,000 accounting firms use our platform

  • 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Over 1,100 Pennylaners from more than 25 nationalities

  • 💰 More than €400 million raised since launch

  • 🌍 Remote-friendly, international culture expanding across Europe

 

What You’ll Do

You will own conversion across the Financial Services and Monetization scope, working across website pages, paid landing pages, product journeys, experimentation, and measurement.

 

Own CRO and Experimentation

  • Define and execute the conversion strategy for key journeys, including pro account landing pages, pricing and product pages, demo-booking journeys, self-sign-up, and upsell flows

  • Build and run a continuous A/B testing program, from ideation and scoping to sizing, analysis, and ship-or-kill decisions

  • Identify conversion friction and opportunities through analytics and behavioral insights

  • Ensure experiments are measured against meaningful business outcomes

 

Manage the Website Conversion Roadmap

  • Own key Financial Services journeys, including pro account activation and the accountant portal

Build and Optimize Paid Landing Pages

Own Measurement and Cross-Functional Coordination

  • Experience managing a roadmap and prioritizing initiatives based on impact and feasibility

  • Strong project management skills, from writing a clear brief to coordinating delivery and measuring results

  • Excellent communication skills, with the ability to:

    • Write clear briefs for designers and engineers

    • Explain prioritization decisions to stakeholders

    • Present results and recommendations to non-technical audiences

  • Ability to build relationships and secure alignment across multiple teams

  • Fluent French and professional English

 

🛠️ Tools and Environment

title: Corporate Paralegal
descriptionHtml:
About Mistral

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.

About the Role

Mistral AI's corporate legal team is looking for a Corporate Paralegal to join our growing legal function in Paris. This is a newly created role designed to centralize and streamline the administrative backbone of our corporate legal operations as we scale internationally.

This is a high-autonomy role. You will own several critical workstreams end-to-end — from KYC and entity housekeeping to cap table management and contract administration — and you will be expected to exercise sound judgment, escalate when needed, and drive automation wherever possible.

What you'll do

1. Cap Table & Share Register

Own the cap table across different systems with rigor and precision. Record all share movements — issuances, transfers, ESOP/BSPCE, funding rounds. Maintain the legal share register and reconcile against articles, shareholders' agreements, and board minutes. Produce cap table extracts, shareholder lists, and ownership reports for KYC, audit, board packs, and investors — always under NDA and with judgment on what can be disclosed. Strong Excel skills (pivot tables, lookups, reconciliation) are essential.

2. Entity Management, Corporate Formalities & Notarisation

Handle entity creation from incorporation to corporate maintenance across jurisdictions (SAS, Inc, Ltd, Pte, GmbH, etc.) with confidentiality and attention to detail. Manage the annual formalities calendar, board/shareholder minutes, resolutions, powers of attorney, and the entity housekeeping file for each group company. Coordinate notarial formalities — share transfers, capital changes, statutory modifications, pledges. Handle apostilles, legalisation, and certified translations for documents used abroad via the Legal Vision Platform. Maintain up-to-date KYC packs for each entity: Kbis, articles, directors, beneficial ownership, administrative certificates. Respond to inbound KYC requests from banks, clients, and investors. Log every formalité for a complete and auditable record.

3. Insurance & Document Management

Manage insurance policies, certificates (COIs), and the renewal calendar. Handle COI requests by checking them against contractual requirements and following up with brokers. Keep a register of policies and claims. File and archive documents with naming conventions and versioning in our document management tools. Manage e-signatures (DocuSign). Maintain the contract register with expiry dates and notice periods. Provide up-to-date insurance certificates and policy summaries as part of KYC documentation for each entity.

4. Procurement Contracts

First-level review of NDAs, order forms, and simple SOWs against Mistral templates, flagging deviations for escalation. Version comparison and clean redlines. Understand the procurement policy to know when legal review is mandatory. Coordinate with Procurement, business teams, and Finance to move deals to signature. Complete supplier onboarding questionnaires (anti-bribery, sanctions, ESG, security) and supplier portals (Ariba, Coupa) as part of the vendor KYC process. Comfortable with tools like Ironclad, Notion, and Slack; keen to automate and reduce manual work.

What you bring

  • 10+ years of experience in a legal field, with a strong preference for corporate law (M&A, banking, funds, or large corporate groups).

  • Experience in a law firm (corporate/M&A/banking), investment fund, bank, or a large multinational group (e.g., CAC 40).

  • Proven experience with KYC processes, questionnaires, and administrative certificates.

  • Strong understanding of confidentiality, data protection (GDPR), and the judgment to know what can and cannot be shared externally.

  • Hands-on experience with cap table management tools (Ledgy, Axiocap) or share register administration.

  • Familiarity with French corporate law (SAS) and international entity structures (Delaware Inc, UK Ltd, Singapore Pte, German GmbH).

  • Experience with contract lifecycle management (CLM) tools and e-signature platforms.

  • Exposure to procurement contract review and vendor onboarding.

  • Fluent in English and French (both written and spoken). Additional languages are a plus.

What We Offer

We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks.

For the most up-to-date details on benefits available in your location, please refer to our Benefits page.

Privacy Policy

title: Creative Technologist
descriptionHtml:
TL;DR - We're seeking an exceptional Design Engineer to build the tooling that makes AI-native brand production actually work at scale. You might call yourself a design engineer, creative technologist or even a full-stack product engineer who cares about craft. Here you’ll be someone who builds real infrastructure specifically in service of brand and creative output, working alongside brand designers who owns taste and direction.

Why Lovable?

Lovable is the software creation platform that gives people the power to act on the problems closest to them. For decades, turning an idea into software required so much capital, technical fluency, and time that many ideas never came to life. Lovable is the counterargument: a platform for all people with ideas, ambition, and problems worth solving. From solopreneurs to small business owners to teams at companies like Adidas and Zendesk, people have built over 60 million projects on Lovable since its launch in November 2024. And we’re just getting started.

We’re building a generational company from Stockholm, with growing teams in London, Boston, New York, and San Francisco. Our team is small, talent-dense, and moving quickly, with a culture rooted in extreme ownership, high velocity, and low-ego collaboration. We look for people who care deeply, ship fast, and are eager to make a dent in the world.

Lovable is one of TIME’s 100 Most Influential Companies and has been recognized on the Forbes AI 50 and CNBC Disruptor 50, reflecting our momentum as one of Europe’s fastest-growing AI companies and one of the most ambitious places to build in this next era of software.

What you'll do

In one sentence: build the front-end surfaces and the AI-generation systems that let Lovable’s brand team produce at scale without losing its taste.

  • Build pipelines connecting image/video generation APIs, internal tooling, and the systems brand and marketing already use (Lovable, Design tools, CMS, the marketing site, Slack)

  • Build internal apps for the brand team - plausibly on Lovable itself, which is both a good dogfooding story and just the fastest way to do it

  • Own reliability and versioning for the AI-generation system so brand output doesn't silently drift in quality or style over time

  • Work closely with a Brand Designer who owns taste and direction - you're building the system that lets their judgment scale, not just executing tickets

  • Constantly evaluate new models, APIs, and generation tooling as the landscape moves, and rebuild pipelines when something better comes along

What we're looking for

  • Solid engineering fundamentals - you have a track record of building, shipping, and maintaining real full-stack software

  • Genuine interest in AI generation systems (image/video models, fine-tuning, prompt pipelines) as a technical problem, not just as a user; you’ve built something with these APIs, even if only for yourself

  • Experience translating scrappy explorations into production-ready systems

  • Some design sensibility is a strong plus - you don’t need to be a designer, but you can tell when output is off-brand without it being spelled out, and you enjoy working closely with people who have strong taste

  • Comfortable building for a function with no internal precedent - you'll be making calls with no playbook to lean on

  • You’ll push the boundaries of what's possible with generative pipelines the way our Design Engineers push the boundaries of the web

Nice to have

  • Experience with Lovable or similar AI-native building tools

  • Prior work on marketing sites, design systems or brand tooling

  • Portfolio or side projects that show both craft and curiosity

Our tech stack

Lovable is built with tools that both humans and AI love:

  • Frontend: React, Tailwind

  • Backend: Golang and Rust

  • Cloud: Cloudflare, GCP, AWS, many LLM and generation providers

  • DevOps & Tooling: GitHub Actions, Grafana, OTEL, infra-as-code (Terraform)

And always on the lookout for what's next, especially in image/video generation APIs and pipelines. You’ll build custom tools in chorus with Lovable, while also contributing to Lovable upstream.

How we hire

  1. Fill in a short form then jump on an intro call with a recruiter.
